column1: # Domain-scale annotations for marker_bin_enrichment.py --annotation-manifest.
#   label<TAB>path_or_url
# WHY DOMAIN-SCALE.  At a 250 kb bin the test is COVERAGE of the bin, so a
# peak-scale set (enhancers, cCREs, TF peaks) covers ~0.1% of a bin and its
# coverage fraction ends up measuring gene density.  Sets worth testing at this
# width are hundreds of kb to Mb.  To use a peak-scale set anyway, turn it into
# a DENSITY track (bp-per-bin or peaks-per-bin, via bedtools) and pass it with
# --signal-track instead of here.
# ALREADY AUTOMATIC.  --genome hg38 and --genome hg19 now fetch these into
# --cache-dir with no entry needed here:
#   PMD, HMD   common partially/highly methylated domains, Zhou et al. Nat
#              Genet 2018.  The 6-column file is split by class, so PMD and HMD
#              are tested separately rather than as their union.
#   ChromHMM   full-stack 100-state segmentation (Vu & Ernst, Genome Biol 2021),
#              hg38 lifted over by the authors, collapsed to ~16 biological
#              groups via the state annotation CSV.  ~39 MB, cached after the
#              first run.
#   LAD        hg19 only (UCSC laminB1Lads, Guelen et al. Nature 2008).
#   CpG islands, cytoBand Giemsa bands, GENCODE genes, GO/KEGG.
# Anything that fails to download is reported and skipped, so a stale line here
# will not stop a run.
# UCSC carries the LaminB1 table for hg19 only.  For hg38, scripts/
# fetch_4dn_damid.py pulls the 4DN LaminB1 DamID-seq bigWigs (250 kb, dam-only
# normalised, replicate mean) for 7 cell types and writes both forms:
#   python scripts/fetch_4dn_damid.py --output-dir lad_hg38 --derive-lad-bed
#   signal_track_flags.txt  the bigWigs as --signal-track (PREFERRED: the score
#                           is log2(Dam-LaminB1/Dam), so >0 is lamina-proximal
#                           and a threshold throws that gradient away).  Use
#                           --normalize zscore, not log2-median -- it is signed.
#   annotation_manifest.tsv cLAD / fLAD / ciLAD as BEDs, for when a discrete
#                           partition is wanted.  cLAD shrinks as cell types
#                           are added, so these are not comparable across runs
#                           with different --cell-type lists.
# NOT LADs: the same 4DN collection has nucleolar-targeting DamID (NADs).  They
# overlap LADs substantially but are a different compartment; the fetcher keeps
# LaminB1-Dam only.
# None of the 7 cell types is meningeal.  cLAD is the cross-cell-type invariant
# part and travels; per-cell-type tracks do not.
# scripts/fetch_4dn_repliseq.py builds log2(early/late) from the 4DN 2-stage
# Repli-seq fractions: 12 human cell types and states, plus three
# genotypes of one engineered iPSC line (15 tracks in all).
#   python scripts/fetch_4dn_repliseq.py --output-dir rt_hg38
# 4DN releases the two fractions SEPARATELY as 5 kb RPKM bedGraphs, not a
# timing track, so the ratio is built here -- at 250 kb, by summing each
# fraction over the bin and then dividing.  At native 5 kb, 14% of early bins
# are zero and a per-bin ratio is mostly pseudocount; ratio-of-totals and
# mean-of-ratios are different numbers and only the first is meaningful.
# --derive-partition-bed adds the CROSS-cell-type classes as BEDs plus an
# annotation_manifest.tsv, so they appear under 'Other annotations':
#   RT_constitutive_late   late in every cell type
#   RT_constitutive_early  early in every cell type
#   RT_variable            late in some, early in others
# A bin counts only where every cell type measured it (coverage differs, and
# scoring a bin "late in all" on three of twelve would make the class largest
# where the data are thinnest).  --rt-threshold opens a dead zone so bins
# hovering at zero are not called variable on noise; with t > 0 the classes
# stop being exhaustive and the leftover count is reported.
# Over 11 distinct cell types: 25.6% constitutive early, 50.6% variable, 23.8%
# constitutive late.  These line up with the LAD partition almost perfectly --
# constitutive-early is 82.7% ciLAD and 0% cLAD, constitutive-late is 74.0%
# cLAD and 0.2% ciLAD, variable is 73.8% fLAD.
# Use signal_track_flags.txt with --signal-track.  Signed, so
# bin_set_signal_summary needs --normalize zscore.  --derive-domain-bed writes
# early/late BEDs at the sign cut for coverage-style tests.
# Sanity check that also validates the LAD fetcher: in HFFc6 this track
# correlates with the 4DN LaminB1 DamID signal at r = -0.84, early being
# lamina-distal.
# scripts/fetch_repeat_density.py turns the UCSC RepeatMasker table into
# per-bin density tracks:
#   python scripts/fetch_repeat_density.py --output-dir repeats --main-chroms-only \
#       --family L1 --family Alu --name L1HS --name AluY
# NOT as --annotation.  A single element is a few hundred bp, so no 250 kb bin
# is ever half covered by one and a region test at majority overlap returns an
# empty table.  What IS domain-scale is their density: pass
# signal_track_flags.txt with --signal-track.
# Sanity check, and a check on the RT and LAD fetchers at the same time: in
# HFFc6 the canonical compartment antagonism comes straight out --
#   SINE/Alu  rho +0.60 vs log2(E/L), -0.59 vs LaminB1   (early, lamina-distal)
#   LINE/L1   rho -0.38 vs log2(E/L), +0.45 vs LaminB1   (late, lamina-bound)
#   DNA       rho +0.07 / +0.02                          (ancient, no preference)
# The young subfamilies are worth separating from their class: L1HS and AluY
# are still mobile and do not sit where the ancient L1M/AluJ copies sit.
# From Hi-C in a relevant line (4DN).  Meningioma arises from arachnoid cap
# cells, so a mesenchymal/fibroblast reference is nearer than a neuronal one.
# compartment_A
# compartment_B
# GISTIC peaks from a published meningioma cohort.  READ THE CNV CAVEAT FIRST:
# celltype_marker_bins.py --cnv-seg tests whether a contrast is copy number
# rather than biology, and a hit here is uninterpretable until that passes.
# meningioma_del
# meningioma_amp
